definition: In mathematical optimization, Lemke's algorithm is a procedure for solving linear complementarity problems, and more generally mixed linear complementarity problems.
details: It is named after Carlton E. Lemke. Lemke's algorithm is of pivoting or basis-exchange type. Similar algorithms can compute Nash equilibria for two-person matrix and bimatrix games.

explainer.lead: Lemke's algorithm is a pivoting procedure for solving linear complementarity problems and their mixed linear variants. It matters because such problems underpin equilibrium and optimization computations, including Nash equilibria in two-person games.

tiers.eli5: It's a step-by-step swapping procedure that keeps adjusting a solution until everything lines up consistently, like rotating players on a team until the lineup fits all the rules.
tiers.practitioner: It is a basis-exchange (pivoting) method in the same family as simplex-style procedures, and analogous algorithms can compute Nash equilibria for two-person matrix and bimatrix games. A practical pitfall is that pivoting methods require careful handling of degeneracy and termination.
tiers.paperLevel: A pivoting or basis-exchange algorithm for solving linear complementarity problems, and more generally mixed linear complementarity problems; named after Carlton E. Lemke.

explainer.example: To find a Nash equilibrium of a two-person bimatrix game, an analogous Lemke-type pivoting algorithm can be run, exchanging bases until an equilibrium is reached.
